section: Environmental Studies · Ch42 — Force, Motion & Energy
subject: Environmental Studies
stem: A book resting on a table remains at rest because the table exerts an upward force equal and opposite to the book's weight. This upward force is called:
explanation: The normal reaction (perpendicular contact force) balances the book's weight, keeping it in equilibrium. Friction acts along the surface, not upward support.

section: Environmental Studies · Ch42 — Force, Motion & Energy
subject: Environmental Studies
stem: A ball is dropped from a height. As it falls, its potential energy decreases while its kinetic energy increases. This best illustrates:

options.option_text: The Law of Conservation of Energy

explanation: Energy is not created or destroyed but converted from one form to another; PE lost equals KE gained, keeping total mechanical energy constant.

section: Environmental Studies · Ch43 — Light, Sound & Electricity
subject: Environmental Studies
stem: A plane mirror always forms an image that is virtual, erect and of the same size as the object, but with one distinguishing feature. That feature is:

options.option_text: Lateral inversion — left and right appear interchanged
The image is always smaller than the object
The image is always inverted (upside down)
The image can be caught on a screen

explanation: Plane mirrors laterally invert images but keep the same size and orientation; the image is virtual and cannot be caught on a screen.

section: Environmental Studies · Ch43 — Light, Sound & Electricity
subject: Environmental Studies
stem: In a string of old-style decorative bulbs wired in series, if one bulb fuses, all the other bulbs go off. This happens because a series circuit:

options.option_text: Provides only a single path for current, which is broken when any one component fails
Provides multiple paths, so failure of one bulb should not matter
Increases voltage across the remaining bulbs to keep them glowing

explanation: A series circuit has only one current path; a break anywhere stops current everywhere in the loop.
